title: Visual Studio stops on handled exceptions while loading an OpenVINO model in C++
body: I am using OpenVINO Runtime 2023.0.1 on 64-bit Windows with Visual Studio 2019 and CPU inference. When I call `core.read_model(model_path)` for my YOLO-NAS-s model, Visual Studio reports a `std::runtime_error`. This happens with the ONNX model and with XML or BIN files, while the model loads normally in Python. I am using the model-loading code from the official documentation.

symptoms_visible: While debugging my C++ application, Visual Studio stops at `core.read_model(model_path)` and reports a Microsoft C++ `std::runtime_error`.
I see the stop with the ONNX model and with XML or BIN files, although the model loads normally in Python.
N0.label: N0 read_model exception reported

symptoms_visible: With OpenVINO 2022.2, reading the model gets past the earlier stop, but Visual Studio reports `InferenceEngine::NotFound` when I call `compile_model()`.
N1.label: N1 behavior checked on 2022.2

symptoms_visible: With OpenVINO 2022.1, the model loads and inference runs without the exception stops I saw in the newer versions.
N2.label: N2 older runtime comparison

symptoms_visible: I traced the PyTorch model to TorchScript, converted it with `convert_model`, serialized the resulting IR, and Visual Studio still stops with the same exception when the C++ application reads it.
N3_x.label: N3_x alternate conversion aftermath

symptoms_visible: After building the provided project in Release mode with OpenVINO 2023.0.1 and running it normally, the model loads and the application executes.
N4.label: N4 standalone Release run succeeds

symptoms_visible: I had Visual Studio exception breakpoints enabled, so the debugger paused whenever OpenVINO threw an exception.
If I disable that break behavior or continue past the reported exceptions, the model loads and the application still works.
N5.label: N5 debugger pause identified

symptoms_visible: With Visual Studio no longer stopping on each thrown C++ exception, `read_model` completes and the OpenVINO C++ application runs inference successfully.
N_terminal.label: terminal debugger behavior resolved

question_patterns: Does the behavior change with an older OpenVINO runtime?
Can you test the same model and C++ code with OpenVINO 2022.2 and describe what you observe around `read_model` and `compile_model`?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With 2022.2, I no longer get the original stop while reading, but Visual Studio reports `InferenceEngine::NotFound` when I use `compile_model()`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The application terminates with an uncaught exception on every tested version, including when run normally without Visual Studio.
The same debugger stop occurs in `compile_model()` rather than `read_model()` on 2022.2.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c4 and c9 compare the same reporter's Windows C++ setup across runtime versions. The answer records only the observed exception and call site.

question_patterns: What happens if you run the same model with OpenVINO 2022.1?
Is there any older runtime version on which loading and inference complete?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I downgraded to 2022.1. I don't get those exception stops there, and inference runs.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: OpenVINO 2022.1 terminates in exactly the same way before the model can load.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c5 and c7: the reporter installed and tested 2022.1. This is version-comparison evidence, not the final recommendation.

solution.intent: Avoid the ONNX frontend by regenerating the IR through the PyTorch frontend, then load the newly serialized XML and BIN files in C++.
solution.concrete_example: Convert the original PyTorch model, or a traced TorchScript form if scripting fails, with `convert_model`; serialize it as XML and BIN and try that IR in the C++ runtime.

edges.comment: Participant4 suggested this in c15-c19. The reporter tried a PyTorch-to-TorchScript-to-IR conversion and serialization in c20-c21, but the debugger showed the same exception stop, so conversion format was not the cause.

question_patterns: Can you build the linked project in Release mode with the documented Windows configuration and run the resulting executable directly?
Please reproduce with the exact Release build commands and report whether the process terminates or produces inference output.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: You're right, it does work. I built and ran the project with OpenVINO 2023.0.1, and the model loads and runs normally.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The Release executable terminates at `read_model` with an uncaught `std::runtime_error` and produces no inference output.
The Release executable completes successfully but takes slightly longer to start.

edges.comment: Participant6 reproduced the reporter's repository successfully in c35. The reporter then ran the same project and confirmed in c36 that it works. This run narrows the issue to the debugging experience rather than model loading.

question_patterns: How are you launching the program when it appears to fail, and does the process actually terminate or merely pause inside Visual Studio?
What Visual Studio debugger settings are active when it stops, and what happens after the pause?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I was debugging in Visual Studio and had the exception breakpoints turned on, so it stopped whenever an exception was thrown. If I disable that and ignore or continue past the exceptions, it still works on 2023.0.1. The debugger lists `std::runtime_error` plus several `InferenceEngine` exception types.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Visual Studio has no break-on-thrown exception setting enabled; the process exits because the exception is uncaught even when I run without the debugger.
Visual Studio is using a dark color theme.

edges.comment: Reporter c36 identifies the decisive distinction: Visual Studio was pausing on thrown exceptions because exception breakpoints were enabled, while the program completed successfully when allowed to run. The successful continuation is additional information volunteered in the same response.

solution.intent: Treat the messages as debugger-visible first-chance exceptions that OpenVINO handles internally, rather than as a failed `read_model` call; configure Visual Studio not to break on every thrown C++ exception or continue past the pause, then verify model loading and inference complete.
solution.concrete_example: In Visual Studio's Exception Settings, stop breaking on every thrown C++ exception, or continue past these pauses. Then rerun the same OpenVINO 2023.0.1 application and confirm that `read_model`, compilation, and inference complete normally. Investigate further only if an exception escapes and terminates the process.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the raw observations that Visual Studio paused with exception breakpoints enabled and that continuing or running the Release executable succeeded. Concluding that these are first-chance exceptions handled inside OpenVINO, rather than uncaught failures from `read_model`, is the diagnostic inference.

edges.comment: Final accepted resolution follows reporter c36: the application works on 2023.0.1 once Visual Studio is not allowed to treat every thrown internal exception as a stopping failure. The later thread contains similar reports but no evidence overturning the reporter's confirmed outcome.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted cause: Visual Studio was pausing on thrown, internally handled first-chance exceptions because exception breakpoints were enabled; `read_model` was not actually terminating the application.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the successful OpenVINO 2023.0.1 Release run and the reporter's observation that continuing or disabling the debugger break behavior lets loading and inference complete.
Must not treat ONNX conversion, regenerated IR, or permanent downgrade to OpenVINO 2022.1 as the fix; the alternate PyTorch/TorchScript-to-IR conversion produced the same debugger stop.
Must distinguish a debugger pause from an uncaught exception that terminates the process, and recommend further investigation if the process truly exits.
Must ask the user to verify that model reading, compilation, and inference complete after adjusting the debugger behavior before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Intermediate C++ and computer-vision developer who can build with Visual Studio and CMake, convert PyTorch and ONNX models, switch OpenVINO versions, and share a reproducible project, but initially interprets Visual Studio first-chance exception pauses as fatal failures.
persona_hint.communication_style: Persistent and evidence-oriented; reports version comparisons and conversion experiments in detail, asks direct implementation questions, and readily corrects the diagnosis after reproducing a successful Release run.
